answer: Proof-of-Work Identity Accrual. Each agent identity earns spending capacity only by completing publicly verifiable compute tasks over time; initial capacity sits at a nadir near zero. A shared vault reconciles task receipts, and rewards flow as nectar proportional to sustained work, not registration. Cloning a new identity therefore costs the full compute and latency to re-accrue capacity from scratch, with no transferable shortcut. Attackers pay roughly N times the per-identity work cost for N clones, making honest long-lived operation strictly cheaper than sybil fan-out.
